chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from al-Mufaḍḍal, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), “Who washed Fāṭimah?”

He said, “That was Amīr al-Muʾminīn.” And it was as though I considered that grave from his statement, so he said, “It is as though you have become constrained by what I informed you of.” He said: So I said, “That has indeed been so; may I be your ransom.”
He said: So he said, “Do not be constrained, for she is a truthful one, and none but a truthful one would wash her. Do you not know that Maryam, none washed her except ʿĪsā?”

key_terms.صِدِّيقَةٌ: a supremely truthful and verified woman
key_terms.عِيسَى: ʿĪsā (عليه السلام), who is cited as the one who washed Maryam
key_terms.غَسَّلَ: performed the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ: Fāṭimah al-Zahrāʾ (عليها السلام), daughter of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم)
key_terms.مَرْيَمَ: Maryam (عليها السلام), invoked here as a parallel example

ai.seo_question: Who washed Fāṭimah al-Zahrāʾ (عليها السلام) according to al-Kāfī?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) washed Fāṭimah (عليها السلام) after her passing. Imām Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) explains that this is fitting because she was a ṣiddīqah, and only a ṣiddīq would wash her, drawing a parallel with Maryam and ʿĪsā (عليهما السلام).
